scope: The standing Qing mansion and Cuijin Garden, with the principal axial gates and halls, courtyard wings, Rear Building, Western-style garden gate, pond pavilion and mapped garden roof groups.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Museum route identifies the gate, courtyards, Yin’an Hall, Baoguang Chamber, Xijin Studio, Rear Building, Western-style Gate, ponds and theatre. It records the 183 m Rear Building, north wall fenestration and marble gate detail.
The Western-style marble gate stands at the south end of the garden’s central path and has a round Western arch.
Grand Theatre is an enclosed brick-and-timber building of 685 square metres. The Peony Garden fronts the plain exterior.
Museum documentation of the 2005–2008 restoration identifies the standing perimeter, wood framing, polychrome treatment and restored Yin’an Hall.
The open Buildings theme provides supplemental roofprint data. The saved tiled source records GERS IDs and East Asian study lineage per polygon.
The museum identifies the four green glazed ceremonial roofs. Upper side ranges have gray tile.
Jiale Hall has five bays, a hard gable, glazed green tiles and a projecting porch.
